image.alt: A Jade Pothos with glossy dark green heart-shaped leaves trailing from a white pot

light.label: Medium to bright indirect light
light.note: Tolerates low light, but growth slows

landscape_use.note: Frost-free zones only; spreads fast, so keep it trimmed

home_use.note: Trails well from a high shelf, even far from a window

snap: A trailing vine with glossy, deep green heart-shaped leaves and no variegation. It copes with dim rooms better than most houseplants and forgives missed waterings. A good first plant for offices and shaded corners. Toxic to cats and dogs if chewed.

deep_dive.title: Origin & Habit
deep_dive.body: The pothos is native to the Society Islands in the South Pacific and now grows wild across the tropics, where it climbs tree trunks with aerial roots. The Jade is a cultivated form with solid green leaves, with none of the cream or yellow markings of other pothos. Indoors the vines trail 2 m or more, or climb a pole or trellis.

deep_dive.title: Key Care Rule
deep_dive.body: Water when the top 3–5 cm of soil is dry, and never leave the pot standing in water. It droops when thirsty and perks up soon after a drink. Yellow, mushy leaves mean too much water. It grows best in medium to bright indirect light but copes with low light, and direct sun scorches the leaves.

deep_dive.title: Special Feature
deep_dive.body: With solid green leaves it has no pattern to fade, so it keeps its rich colour even in a dim room. That makes it one of the most reliable plants for offices and shaded corners. Cuttings with a node root easily in a glass of water. Trim the vine tips to keep it full, and give it a moss pole to climb for larger leaves.
